top.line: Unexplained agent bills are an engineering defect to fix
top.para: A business plan for a service that helps companies manage agentic AI cost by observing what already exists. Agents shipped from the explorer side, with logs and invoices nobody reads together and no cost owner. The service installs nothing, builds footprints, a twin and policies, and returns two lists: what to stop paying for and what to build.

short.line: Existing logs, read together, yield cost and build lists
short.para: Unexplained bills come from estates grown in sessions without policy, twin, owner or cap. Invoices, traces and prompts read together give each agent a footprint. The service returns a cost list and an engineering list, treats missing data as findings, moves data through vaults, and offers four price levels plus a share-of-savings option.

problem.line: Agents built as explorers run on commodities nobody reconciles
problem.para: Agents usually grow from a session prompt into production, the explorer side of the map, while running on commodity model APIs billed exactly. Invoices, logs and traces exist but nobody reads them together, and no one owns cost. Loops, whole-context calls and keys without ceilings are defects engineers fix once visible.

service.line: Observe, map footprint, twin and policy, then find savings
service.para: Customers drop invoices, traces, prompts and schedules into their own sealed vault. The service builds each agent's footprint, a twin of the estate with cost on every edge, and the policy each agent actually ran under. It then lists savings, such as context cut by ninety per cent, and engineering opportunities.

positive.line: Sell cost reduction, deliver engineering opportunity
positive.para: A cost review is bought once and resented; a map of what to build brings customers back. The same logs that show a loop show the workflow worth building, and shared prompts reveal missing components. Gaps such as unlogged agents or unowned keys are the first findings most companies need.

vaults.line: Vaults fit capture, transformation and movement of the data
vaults.para: Customers encrypt logs into a vault they own and can revoke, and the service holds only a read key. Every step from invoice to finding is a commit, so findings trace back to source lines. Anonymised extracts leave as sealed envelopes to a benchmark vault, after the customer sees them.

money.line: Four price levels from £50 to Tailored, all assumptions
money.para: The kit costs £50, a self-run cost vault £250, a Standard estate read £3,000 within ten working days, and Tailored from £9,000, with a share-of-savings alternative. About eight Standard and two Tailored engagements a month would cover a two-founder burn. Every number is a labelled assumption.

exists.line: The methods exist; parsers, catalogue and customers do not
exists.para: The footprint method, behaviour policy format, connector twin design, vault tooling, sealed envelopes and Company X-Ray pattern already exist. Missing are the cost analysis catalogue, the agent estate twin schema, log parsers, the benchmark vault and any customer. That is a few weeks of work.

limits.line: No estate read yet; prices and map are sketches
limits.para: The two lists describe what is expected, not found, and the prices are assumptions to test on the first three customers. The Wardley map is an argument, not a measurement. Share of savings needs an invoice baseline and agreed attribution before anyone signs.

sources.line: Sources: a voice memo and earlier site articles
sources.para: Written from a 12 October 2026 voice memo after a conversation with an unnamed potential collaborator. It builds on Footprint and blast radius, The behaviour policy is the business logic, Connector Twin, The agent is the reader, Every mistake added a rule, RFC 0001 and the business plans page.
